To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the data are compatible with the expected signal from a candidate with mixed couplings to ordinary matter.

the annual modulation effect in the DAMA data can be explained in terms of a candidate with mixed couplings, and that the data are compatible with a WIMP candidate with mixed coupling to ordinary matter.
, in the framework of a WIMP candidate with mixed coupling, the data of DAMA/LIBRA and of the other experiments are compatible and that a WIMP candidate is not excluded.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following points: (1) the possibility to explain the annual modulation data with the mixed coupling framework; (2) the possibility of discriminating between the different scenarios of mixed coupling; (3) the possibility that a candidate with mixed couplings could mimic the annual modulation effect.
the possibility that WIMPs could couple to ordinary matter via a mixture of scalar and pseudoscalar interactions.
(a) a general analysis of the DAMA data, performed in a mixed coupling model; (b) a comparison with data from other direct detection experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are compatible with the expected signature of the modulation effect induced by a WIMP annual modulation signal in case of a candidate with a mixed coupling.

, within the framework considered, the data are compatible with the presence of a WIMP annual modulation component and, at the same time, are not compatible with the presence at the same time of an annual modulation component due to a candidate with mixed couplings and of an annual modulation signal due to the solar neutrino elastic scattering.
, if a WIMP component is responsible for the annual modulation signal observed by the DAMA collaboration, it is necessary to consider mixed coupling to ordinary matters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the DAMA annual modulated signal is compatible with being due to a candidate with a mixed coupling to ordinary matters, and that the present experimental results are not conclusive to exclude a candidate with a purely spin-independent coupling to ordinary matters.
the DAMA annual modulating signal is not compatible with a mixed coupling WIMP candidate, if we assume that the WIMP-nucleus interaction cross section is dominated by scalar or axial-vector coupling.

, if the DAMA data are interpreted in terms of a candidate with mixed couplings, the DAMA annual modulated component is not compatible with a WIMP candidate with pure axial coupling to ordinary matter, but is compatible with candidates with mixed couplings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in this framework, the DAMA annual cycle data are compatible with a light WIMP (≃9 GeV/c2) with mixed couplings to the ordinary matter, which is not compatible with other experimental results.

, if the annual modulation signal is due to a WIMP with mixed coupling, the DAMA annual cycle data are not able to exclude any value of the WIMP coupling to ordinary matter, and the DAMA annual modulations are compatible with the annual modulation signals of other experiments, including the CoGeNT and CRESST experiments.
, in this framework, a WIMP with mixed coupling to matter can be consistent with the DAMA annual modulated data, even in the absence of other positive experimental results.
